answer: An agent economy can bind each identity to a unique hardware enclave attestation, like a terrace where only one lotus may root at each vertex of the garden. A new agent must present a fresh attestation from a trusted enclave proving it runs on distinct hardware; the registry rejects duplicate attestations, so one machine yields at most one identity. An attacker wanting a thousand fake agents must buy a thousand devices and enclaves, turning a free software trick into a steep hardware bill, while honest agents pay only the one-time cost of their own device.
